summary: The Rhodes Scholarship is a postgraduate award for full-time study at the University of Oxford in almost any field, run by the Rhodes Trust. It is open through country or regional 'constituencies', each with its own citizenship, residence, age and school rules, and is chosen by written application, a social event and an interview. It pays Oxford course fees, a living stipend, visa and health-surcharge costs, flights and a settling-in allowance. The usual length is two years, with one-year tenure for professional degrees and longer tenure for some doctorates. Applications are closed now and the Trust says they reopen in 2027 for entry in 2028.
eligibility_notes:
Constituency: eligibility depends on the constituency (a country or group of countries) the applicant applies through, not on nationality alone. The Trust lists 24 active constituencies: Australia, Bermuda, Canada, China, Commonwealth Caribbean, East Africa (Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, South Sudan, Burundi), Germany, Hong Kong SAR, India, Israel, Jamaica, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Southern Africa (South Africa, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia, eSwatini), Syria/Jordan/Lebanon/Palestine, the United Arab Emirates, the USA and its territories, West Africa (Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Cote d'Ivoire, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Sao Tome and Principe, Togo), Zambia and Zimbabwe. The Commonwealth Caribbean constituency covers Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, the Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, the British Virgin Islands, the Cayman Islands, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Montserrat, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Trinidad and Tobago and the Turks and Caicos Islands. The Global constituency is suspended by the Trustees. People with ties to more than one constituency should apply where the connection is strongest (citizenship or long-term residence); a person with strong ties to two or more but who meets none can ask for Inter-Jurisdictional Consideration, which waives some rules but not age, English or academic achievement.

Examples of constituency rules (2027 entry cycle): India requires Indian citizenship (PIO and OCI card holders do not count; refugees and asylum seekers in India are considered), formal study in India for at least 4 of the last 10 years, and either a school-leaving exam in India or a final-year or completed degree at an Indian university. East Africa requires citizenship of Burundi, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania or Uganda and at least five of the last ten years in one or more of those countries or in Kenya. Check the constituency page for the 2028 cycle once it is published.

Academic: the applicant must complete an undergraduate degree (normally a bachelor's) by the following July and have a background and grade that at least meet the entry requirements of the chosen full-time Oxford course. A First Class degree or equivalent, or a GPA of 3.70/4.0 or higher, raises the chance of admission. Some constituencies set a minimum GPA. Applicants must also meet Oxford's higher-level English requirement unless they qualify for a test waiver (rules vary by constituency; non-native speakers must meet Oxford's higher level for their course).

Selection criteria: literary and scholastic attainment, energy to use one's talents fully, truth, courage, devotion to duty and care for others, and moral force of character with instincts to lead.

Limits: one application per year; an unsuccessful candidate may reapply once through the same constituency, and no more than two applications in total. The USA and Canada constituencies require an institutional endorsement from a senior official; the Global constituency required a nomination letter from the applicant's university. Current Oxford postgraduates may apply only for a new course, not to fund the rest of the current one. Selection is made without regard to financial means, marital status, race, religion, sexual orientation or disability.
age_experience_notes: Age limits are set by constituency and strictly applied. For the 2027 entry cycle, India: aged 18 to 23 on 1 October 2026, or under 27 on that date with the first undergraduate degree completed on or after 1 October 2025. East Africa: aged 18 to 24 on 1 October 2026, or under 27 with the first undergraduate degree completed on or after 1 July 2025. Southern Africa for the same cycle was at least 19 and not past the 25th birthday on entry to Oxford (carried over from stored data; not re-read). The Trust may consider case-by-case exceptions for people who narrowly miss the limit because of war in their country; they should contact their National Secretary. Age limits for the 2028 cycle are not published yet. No work experience is required.
funding_summary: The Trust pays Oxford course fees and a stipend. For 2026-27 the stipend is GBP 21,060, paid as GBP 1,755 a month, and it must cover all living costs including accommodation; it is not enough for partners or dependants. The Trust also pays the Oxford application fee, the student visa fee and the Immigration Health Surcharge, two economy flights to and from the UK, and a settling-in allowance. Standard tenure is two years. Professional degrees are one year only, direct-entry DPhil support is up to three years, and a 1+3 route gets up to four years. Support continues only with satisfactory academic progress and personal conduct.
programmes_note: Scholars may take almost any full-time postgraduate degree at Oxford (a postgraduate diploma or certificate does not count). Standard two-year choices are a two-year MPhil or BPhil, a two-year MSc by Research, two successive one-year taught master's degrees (such as MSc, MSt, MFA, BCL) with limits, or a second BA with Senior Status over two years. Professional degrees such as the MPP, MBA and MFE are available only as a one-year tenure and are limited each year. Not funded: part-time courses, PGCert and PGDip courses (including the PGCE), the accelerated four-year graduate-entry Medicine course, the DClinPsych and other courses requiring NHS employment, and the MPhil-to-DPhil route (five-year fee liability). Integrated four-year doctoral training programmes count only if another funder pays at least one year. Applicants name a main course and a back-up course.
institutions_note: University of Oxford only. The Trust supports selected candidates in applying to Oxford after selection; the Scholarship is confirmed only once Oxford admission is secured. Admission requires meeting the entry requirements of the chosen course, and some courses close in early December.

summary.detail: Master's study at Oxford normally lasts two years under the standard tenure: a two-year MPhil or BPhil, a two-year MSc by Research, or two successive one-year taught master's degrees. One-year tenure is available for professional degrees (MPP, MBA, MFE) and other one-year master's degrees where it suits the scholar. Fees and stipend are paid for up to 24 months (standard) or 12 months (one-year).

summary.detail: DPhil (PhD) at Oxford. Direct entry: fees and stipend for up to three years, available to those with a master's qualification in any division, and usually to those with only an undergraduate degree in the Science Divisions. 1+3 route: a one-year master's, then DPhil, supported for up to four years. Doctoral tenure is approved after selection by the Rhodes Academic Review Board in a further competitive process, and Scholars should also hold a two-year standard-tenure plan. Many DPhils take 3 to 4 years, so the Scholar must plan how to fund the rest.

requirements.text: Online application form with the applicant's details, evidence of meeting the eligibility rules, education history and the proposed Oxford course(s). There is no application fee. A main and a back-up course are named.

Birth certificate or valid passport showing the age requirement is met, and a passport or equivalent proof of citizenship (the India guide names a voter ID as an example). Documents not in English need official English translations; originals may be asked for later.

Official transcript from the university studied at, with grades to date. The India guide also asks for transcripts or marksheets of the 10th and 12th standard school exams, and evidence of formal study in India for at least 4 of the last 10 years for those who are not Indian graduates.
requirements.conditional_rule: School transcripts and the residency evidence follow the constituency rules (example: India)

requirements.text: Academic statement of study: your reasons for Oxford, your chosen courses, how you meet or exceed the course requirements, and for a DPhil a short outline of the research area, the department and the researchers you would like to work with. The limit was 450 words in the India guide and 350 words in the Global guide.

Personal statement of no more than 1,000 words in the applicant's own voice, addressing three prompts: which Rhodes quality you show most strongly and how others help you grow in the rest; what you want to learn from and give to the Rhodes community at Oxford; and how you will use your energy and talents on humanity's challenges. Generative AI must not write substantive content.

CV completed inside the application form (separate CV uploads are not accepted in the Global guide). The Global guide allows up to 5 entries in each of five areas: work and research experience, volunteering and leadership, publications and presentations, awards and scholarships, skills and activities.

Four referees in the India and Global guides: three academics who taught and graded you (they give an estimated class ranking) and one character referee who can speak to service, extracurricular activity and leadership. References are confidential, in English, submitted online by the reference deadline. Referees should not normally be friends, peers or relatives. The number of referees varies by constituency; check the 2028 guide.

Evidence of Oxford's higher-level English requirement (a recognised test such as TOEFL or IELTS), or a short letter asking for a waiver, for example because the degree was taught in English. Rules vary by constituency; the India guide says non-native speakers must check they meet the requirement.
requirements.conditional_rule: Applicants whose first language is not English

requirements.text: Head-and-shoulders colour photograph in JPG format. It is hidden from the selectors until final shortlisting and used on the Scholars' pages if selected.

Institutional endorsement or nomination letter from a senior official of the applicant's university (President, Dean, Rector or Vice-Provost). Mandatory in the USA and Canada constituencies according to the FAQ and was required for Global.

application_steps.title: Pick your constituency and check the rules
application_steps.detail: Enter your country in the Trust's eligibility checker. If you have ties to several countries, choose the one you are strongest connected to (citizenship or long-term residence); if you meet none, ask about Inter-Jurisdictional Consideration. Age, residence, school and degree rules differ by constituency. Applications are closed now and reopen in 2027 for entry in 2028.

application_steps.title: Prepare the application and arrange referees
application_steps.detail: Write the academic statement and a personal statement of up to 1,000 words, complete the CV section, collect transcripts and identity documents, choose a main and a back-up Oxford course, and register your referees early. The applicant is responsible for making sure references arrive before the reference deadline. There is no fee.

application_steps.title: Submit the online form to the Rhodes Scholarship first
application_steps.detail: Apply to the Rhodes Scholarship before you apply to Oxford. Only an online application is accepted. An unsuccessful candidate may reapply once in the same constituency, and only one application per year is allowed.

application_steps.title: Eligibility check, longlist and preliminary interview
application_steps.detail: Applications are checked for eligibility and completeness and a longlist is made. Longlisted candidates may be invited to a preliminary interview (video or in person) and sometimes a semi-final interview, which the India guide places in September or October. Format varies by constituency.

application_steps.title: Social engagement event and final interview
application_steps.detail: Finalists attend a reception and meal with panelists, former Rhodes Scholars and other candidates (informal, not scored) and a final panel interview that usually lasts 30 to 45 minutes. All in-person stages are required, and AI tools are banned during the interviews. The Trust may pay a domestic travel allowance for finalists. Selection is made only after an interview.

application_steps.title: Outcome
application_steps.detail: All applicants are emailed the result; the India guide expected this by December 2026 for the 2027 entry cycle. No feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants. The decision of the Selection Committee is final, and no selection is made if no suitably qualified candidate is found.

application_steps.title: Apply to Oxford with Rhodes House support
application_steps.detail: A selected Scholar-elect applies to Oxford straight after selection, with help from Rhodes House, which can see the Rhodes application and may reuse the references. Some courses have early December deadlines (for example the MPP, some Medical Sciences courses and research degrees in Computer Science or Engineering). The Scholarship is confirmed only once Oxford admission is secured. Doctoral tenure needs a further approval by the Rhodes Academic Review Board.

application_steps.title: Arrive at Oxford and keep to the Conditions of Tenure
application_steps.detail: Scholars arrive in late September of the year after selection (selected in 2026 means start in October 2027). The Scholarship cannot be deferred or brought forward, save in the most exceptional circumstances. Continuing tenure depends on satisfactory academic progress and personal conduct. Part-time work is allowed within student visa rules, and partners and dependants may come only for a DPhil or research master's.

fetch_problems: The 2028-entry constituency guides were not available. The India and Global information documents for earlier cycles were read as examples of document lists and selection stages.
The Kenya, India and East Africa 2027 documents surfaced by search were only partly read: the Kenya guide was not opened, so its referee count is not stated here.
The Rhodes House overview page does not link the Conditions of Tenure; it was found through search and read from the Trust's own file.
notes: The Rhodes Scholarship overview page still shows the 2025-26 stipend (GBP 20,400, GBP 1,700 a month), while the Trust's FAQ shows GBP 21,060 (GBP 1,755 a month) for 2026-27. The newer figure is used above; the stored GBP 20,400 is out of date.
A 2024 version of the Conditions of Tenure allowed the MFE and MBA in the second year; the September 2026 version says professional degrees are one-year tenure only. The 2026 version is used.
Stored 'Global constituency shown as suspended' is re-confirmed on the Trust's Global page, which says the Trustees suspended Global scholarships with immediate effect.

The Second BA with Senior Status is a standard tenure option in the Conditions of Tenure, so a bachelor-level route exists at Oxford; the editors may want to mention it, but the stored levels are master and doctorate only.

The number of scholarships per constituency on the Trust's page for the current cycle: Australia 9, Bermuda 1, Canada 11, China 4, Commonwealth Caribbean 1, East Africa 1, Germany 2, Hong Kong SAR 1, India 5, Israel 2, Jamaica 1, Kenya 2, Malaysia 1, New Zealand 3, Pakistan 2, Saudi Arabia 2, Singapore 1, Southern Africa 10, Syria/Jordan/Lebanon/Palestine 2, UAE 2, USA 32, West Africa 3, Zambia 2, Zimbabwe 2.
